title: Omni / Lit: prove the MDU economics property by property
lede: Omni has a documented MDU sales and access process, plus one qualified property-manager listing that markets fiber availability. The reviewed public record does not yet establish a signed MDU portfolio, a bulk-contract base or superior property economics. The pitch should make those claims conditional on the property book. [M01] [M02] [M03]
scope: Omni and integrated Lit operations are the subject of this analysis. Socket and IdeaTek remain a separate sponsor-platform case. A property listing, blank agreement or municipal right-of-way is not a verified contract, installed-unit schedule or customer base.

sections.title: The defensible pitch today
paragraphs: The strongest proposition is an operating process that could turn property access into recurring service revenue. Omni markets a community-development channel and publishes a long-term right-of-entry agreement. A property manager also lists Omni availability at an identified Mansfield apartment. Those are tangible capability signals; they do not measure execution across a portfolio. [M01] [M02] [M03]

Present three separate commercial structures: retail resident sales under signed access agreements; property-paid bulk service under an executed billable-unit schedule; and carrier wholesale service under a separately negotiated customer-ownership, capex and service-level contract. The public materials do not establish an existing Omni bulk or carrier-MDU book. [M01] [M02]
bullets: Value contracted, ready and billable units separately. Accessible units are not automatically customers or revenue.
Tie any MDU premium to assignable rights, installation conversion, retention and property contribution after the full cost of serving the property.
Use municipal P3 capability as a separate origination and operating credential. It does not convey private building access. [M06] [M09]

sections.title: Five named evidence cases and their limits
paragraphs: The strongest property signal is an undated, live Dream Huge Property Management listing for a specific unit at 1885 Chapelwood Drive in Mansfield. It uses the Sunset Blvd Apartments label and says Omni is available. Confirm the property grouping and executed agreement before assigning a building-wide unit count. [M03]

rows: Sunset Blvd Apartments, 1885 Chapelwood Drive Apt. 4; Mansfield, Ohio
One specifically listed apartment unit; no primary-source total property-unit count
Named, property-manager-published evidence that Omni availability is being marketed at a specific apartment unit. [M03]
No executed ROE, building-wide installation, active subscription, bulk billing, exclusive access, property-wide unit count, or economics. The property label and street address require reconciliation.
City of Brownsville and Lit Fiber-BTX municipal network agreements; Brownsville, Texas
Approximately 95 to 100 middle-mile route miles in FY2025 reporting; no MDU unit count
Long-term P3 operating capability, public middle-mile access, and a commercialization structure. [M06] [M07]

A city agreement is not an executed building ROE. Customer-linked city revenue share is not evidence of a property-owner MDU revenue share or bulk contract. No reviewed source separates single-family from MDU units.
Medina Fiber partnership with Medina County Fiber Network; Villages of Seville and Westfield Center and Guilford Township, Medina County, Ohio
First phase described as nearly $8 million; no dwelling-unit or MDU-building count
Lit-originated public-network development and a defined residential launch geography. [M09]
The promise to reach residents does not identify apartment properties, executed ROEs, contracted units, ready units, or bulk billing.
Louisville Ordinance 25-35 public-ways agreement discussion; Louisville, Ohio

Council minutes discuss 14 fiber distribution hubs plus one active cabinet, and an Omni representative described 300 to 500 homes per hub. These are network-planning statements, not MDU units, and are not summed here.
Municipal construction planning and public-right-of-way access at the network level. [M10]
Public-way authority does not grant entry into apartment buildings, establish property-owner consent, or identify dwelling-unit readiness or subscribers.
City of Monroe fiber expansion; Monroe, Michigan
Omni described by the city as planning a nearly citywide build; no exact address or dwelling-unit count
A live municipal construction process in an Omni market. [M11]
Public easements and neighborhood construction do not equal apartment-building access, in-building wiring, whole-property readiness, or MDU penetration.

sections.title: Underwrite the executed agreements
paragraphs: The form currently linked from Omni’s MDU page has a 20-year initial term, annual renewals, and 60-day nonrenewal notice. It grants installation, maintenance, access and resident-marketing rights, with equipment owned by Omni and a covenant running with the land. The older July-path form contemplates perpetual access. Both are blank templates: neither establishes the terms of any executed property contract, and the newer link does not amend earlier contracts. [M01] [M02] [M04]

The current blank form does not specify an executed property, certified unit count, bulk billing, property compensation, minimum billable units, service levels, deployment budget or property economics. Treat those as separate diligence requests. The form does not establish exclusive access. [M02]
bullets: Obtain the signed agreement and all schedules for each property: legal owner, term, renewal, assignment, termination, access, marketing and equipment rights.

For property payments and access restrictions, obtain counsel review of the executed agreement and applicable provider classification. The reviewed federal common-carrier rule addresses exclusive access and certain compensation arrangements; exclusive marketing has disclosure requirements and is not categorically banned. [M12] [M13] [M15]
Separate city revenue sharing from property-owner compensation. Brownsville’s municipal operating arrangements do not disclose an apartment bulk contract. [M06] [M07]

sections.title: Carrier precedents: safe claims and Omni proof required
paragraphs: These public precedents show how carriers have divided network ownership, retail customers, construction and wholesale payments. They do not establish carrier interest in Omni, an Omni contract, or proposed transaction terms. Acquisition dollars, customers, passings and contracted or bulk-billed units remain separate denominators.

The base-case rule is simple: give no credit for carrier revenue, reimbursement, customer-book value or exclusivity until the applicable rights, units, rates, address election and closing status are documented. Unsigned opportunities may be shown only as contingent scenarios. [CR01] [CR02] [CR14] [CR15]

rows: T-Mobile / Lumos and Metronet

Lumos closed April 1, 2025: T-Mobile invested $932 million for 50% of the JV and 97,000 fiber customers. Metronet closed July 24, 2025: $4.6 billion for 50% and 713,000 fiber customers. T-Mobile owns the disclosed retail relationships; the JVs select markets, build and install. Fiber retail revenue, wholesale access cost and installation-fee amortization are separately reported. Lumos anticipates about $500 million more in 2027-2028; the Metronet no-further-contribution statement applies only to its existing business plan. [CR01] [CR02] [CR03] [CR04]

These are acquisition-date customer counts, not September 2026 customers, passings or contracted MDU units. The investment covers a JV interest plus customers and is not a disclosed customer-book price or precedent Omni multiple.

Customer and unit bridge; legal-entity and asset schedule; retail and wholesale product rights; signed MSA; address election; installation fees, recurring rates, minimums, SLA remedies and transfer consents.
Verizon / Eaton and pending Ripple transaction

Verizon disclosed residential exclusivity through the build plus an unspecified additional period. Eaton funds, builds, installs, maintains and operates. July 2026 counterparties described residential and small-business exclusivity and announced $1.5 billion invested in Eaton. Their pending Ripple transaction would also give Verizon the existing customer book and a small network/asset portion adjacent to or partly within Verizon’s North and South Carolina footprint. [CR05] [CR06]

Ripple was announced and remained unverified as closed in the bounded review. The $1.5 billion is not all construction capex or a disclosed all-equity instrument. The sources do not establish perpetual or enterprise-wide exclusivity, zero Verizon investment, an absolute no-overlap rule, or applicability to Omni.

Executed MSA and address schedule; exclusivity by product, address and date; customer and network carveout; cost-to-complete; carrier payments; closing evidence; change-of-control and assignment rights.
AT&T / Lumen Mass Markets and Forged Fiber

AT&T completed the Lumen Mass Markets fiber acquisition on February 2, 2026. The June filing placed the network in wholly owned Forged Fiber 37 Services, LLC and retained customer relationships in Advanced Connectivity. AT&T’s July 22 release still described a planned controlling-interest sale to an equity partner. That separate control sale was not verified closed. Gigapower is a different JV that closed in 2023. [CR11] [CR12] [CR13] [CR15] [CR16]
Held-for-sale or discontinued-operations accounting is not legal closing evidence. The record does not identify the equity partner or establish an Omni transaction.
Separate acquisition close from subsequent control sale; obtain closing evidence, asset and customer allocation, retained liabilities, retail election, wholesale terms and transition services.
Verizon / Starry customer scale

Verizon closed the Starry acquisition January 30, 2026. The October 2025 announcement reported nearly 100,000 MDU customers across five cities. Starry’s historical Customer Relationships definition included individual sign-ups and units billed under bulk arrangements; Homes Serviceable estimated households in deployed-network coverage. [CR07] [CR08] [CR10]

Nearly 100,000 is an announcement-date company figure, not a verified closing or current count, contracted-unit inventory, FTTH passing count, or all individually activated and billed households. The 2025 release may not use the 2021 definition.
Reconcile individual activations separately from bulk-billed units and bridge contracted, accessible, serviceable, ready, installed, billed and active units by property and date.
Starry / Related property rights

The May 22, 2018 master specified March 22, 2024 as its termination date. It required building agreements and suitability review, gave Related 90-day termination rights, preserved Active Agreements under their own terms and included specified assignment exceptions. [CR09]

The master’s stated March 2024 termination date does not prove that every building agreement expired. Schedules and form exhibits are redacted, while current amendments, surviving agreements and post-restructuring rights remain unknown.

Executed building agreements and amendments; property and unit schedules; term, renewal and termination; access, riser, rooftop and wiring rights; equipment ownership; assignment, survival and required consents.
Carrier election and contracted economics

AT&T has disclosed third-party open-access agreements with selective retail election, and its Ubiquity arrangement targeted multifamily and HOA access in stated areas. These precedents support diligence questions only. [CR14] [CR15]
They do not show carrier election of Omni locations, an Omni wholesale rate, minimum revenue, SLA, physical route, diverse connection or enterprise availability.

Dated accepted-address list; explicit passing and ready-for-service definitions; signed MSA or term sheet; recurring and installation fees; billable lines; minimums, escalation, audit, credits, term and termination compensation.

sections.title: Pitch claim ladder: capability, geography and pace
paragraphs: The public record supports a repeatable MDU access process, selected middle- and upper-income pockets and substantial build execution. It does not support a scaled exclusive MDU base, a uniformly affluent footprint or a faster-than-plan or faster-than-peer claim.

Demographic figures below join provider-reported FCC D25 residential-capable FTTP availability locations for Omni legal filer 480067 to 2020-2024 ACS block groups. They are availability-location-weighted averages of reported closed-interval block-group median household income in 2024 dollars, not a household, customer or footprint median. FCC locations are not passings, housing units or subscribers. [P01] [P02]

rows: Strong MDU capability
Omni has a standardized access and resident-marketing process and one named property-manager-published apartment availability signal. [M02] [M03]

The signal is one listed Mansfield apartment unit; property total is undisclosed. The current blank ROE provides a 20-year initial term plus annual renewals and access, installation, equipment and resident-sales provisions.
The reviewed sources establish no executed-property roster, installed-unit base, exclusivity, bulk billing, MDU subscribers, revenue or EBITDA. Avoid “proven, exclusive, scaled MDU platform.”
Attractive household income and geographies
Ohio and Texas contain meaningful middle- and upper-income pockets, while the four-state measured footprint is mixed. [P01] [P02]

Weighted block-group income context: Ohio $74,525 on 150,632 valid-income locations of 157,362 D25 locations; Texas $72,221 on 23,265 of 25,438; Michigan $68,408 on 5,396 of 5,675; Pennsylvania $65,507 on 18,370 of 19,378. The share of valid locations in block groups at or above $90,000 is 23.60%, 23.71%, 20.42% and 12.85%, respectively. All D25 locations matched to ACS block groups; missing or open-ended income observations are excluded from income statistics.

The U.S. median household income is $80,734, but it is not the same statistic as a location-weighted average of block-group medians. Citizens/Kecksburg remains separate and Lit filer identity remains unresolved. Avoid “uniformly affluent footprint” or any customer-income claim.
Faster build pace

Omni demonstrated substantial construction execution: Stonepeak reported 110,000 homes passed in less than two years as of December 31, 2024, and Omni reported about 60 communities serving customers plus about 25 under construction by December 1, 2025. [P03] [P05]

The lender slide describes Omni in Ohio, Michigan and Pennsylvania; Lit/Texas inclusion is not established. July 2024 reported more than 25 communities served and more than 15 under construction, but the later comparison spans the Lit merger. [P04] [P05]

About 200,000 locations for year-end 2024 and 340,000 for year-end 2025 were targets. The reviewed sources establish no verified year-end 2025 actual or peer-normalized rate. Avoid “faster than plan,” “achieved 200,000/340,000,” or “industry-leading pace.”

sections.title: Illustrative economics: contribution can coexist with poor cash recovery
paragraphs: These three deliberately hypothetical retail-access cohorts are not estimates for Omni, Lit or any other operator. They show why direct contribution alone is insufficient: slower conversion can leave simple capital recovery far beyond an attractive holding period. Cohorts have different sizes and cost assumptions; they are scenarios, not measured peers.

Annual direct contribution equals subscriber revenue less property payments and direct service/building costs. It excludes corporate overhead and is not EBITDA. Initial capex includes all accessible-unit in-building costs plus installation cost per activated subscriber.

Five-year cash recovery solves subscriber-dependent installation cost explicitly: required accounts = (five years of fixed property/building cost + in-building capex) divided by (five years of contribution per subscriber before fixed costs minus installation cost per subscriber). Required accounts are rounded upward. The model assumes accounts are present from day one and does not include ramp, churn, replacement capex, tax or financing.

rows: downside: slow conversion
22.03 years
44.12% (75 subscribers minimum)
base: moderate conversion
3.48 years

sections.title: The six files that turn the hypothesis into a pitch
bullets: Executed property agreements and a certified unit schedule, with versions and assignment requirements.
A dated bridge from signed units to accessible, ready-for-service, bulk-billed and active retail units; reconcile property addresses and double counting.
Monthly revenue, property fees, service costs, bad debt and retention by property cohort, separating recurring contribution from allocated EBITDA.
Itemized feeder, entrance, riser, unit-drop, ONT, gateway and remediation capex, including who pays and who owns each component.
For bulk or carrier proposals: billable-unit definitions, vacancy, minimum commitments, customer ownership, SLAs, capex funding and termination liabilities.
Evidence of route serviceability and in-building readiness for each named property; a city-level build announcement or FCC location record is insufficient.
